sections_target.text: This document outlines the steps of the half-yearly inspection of the automatic fire-fighting system in the turbine hall.

There is a complete fire-fighting system using CO2 with 32 cylinders distributed in two parts, one for the control cabinets and auxiliaries and the other for the turbine itself; each part consists of 16 cylinders.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Hani El-Oqda, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, accepted by Eng. Mohamed El-Sherif, General Manager of Instruments, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Meguid Sawan, Head of El-Nubaria Power Station Sector.

The document was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Gelil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the company's Maintenance Procedure Information System coordinator, and certified by Eng. Mohamed Naguib Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; those carrying out the maintenance work must hold an occupational safety and health category card.
Cordon off the area to define the work area, and place warning signs.
Follow the occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment, and wear personal protective equipment (safety helmet, safety shoes, overalls, gloves .....)
Complete tool bag
Cleaning fluids
Make sure the number of cylinders in the system is complete (32) cylinders
Check the response of the suspension weights (counterweights) to movement.

Inspect the mechanical weights placed on the distributor to ensure the system is ready and stable and operates when needed, since there are four common cylinders: if the weight of any one of them drops, discharge to the remaining cylinders takes place.
Make sure the electrical connections are sound.
Make sure all the levers are engaged with the cylinder valves.
Make sure the fire system monitoring panel works properly.

Make sure the 
 Pressure indicator 
 on the 
 Fire line works properly.
Make sure the fire detectors are sound.
Make sure the fire system lines are sound.
Make sure the release cabinet is prepared according to the operating instructions.

Test the 
 Solenoid
 valve 
, making sure it is clean and working.
Make sure the CO2 gas discharge nozzles work properly, and maintain them if necessary.

Introduction
This document outlines the steps of the half-yearly inspection of the automatic fire-fighting system in the turbine hall.
There is a complete fire-fighting system using CO2 with 32 cylinders distributed in two parts, one for the control cabinets and auxiliaries and the other for the turbine itself; each part consists of 16 cylinders.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Hani El-Oqda, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, accepted by Eng. Mohamed El-Sherif, General Manager of Instruments, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Meguid Sawan, Head of El-Nubaria Power Station Sector.
The document was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Gelil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the company's Maintenance Procedure Information System coordinator, and certified by Eng. Mohamed Naguib Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
